title: Man dies in police custody
article: A bus passenger who was injured while resisting arrest by RCMP in British Columbia has died, the second in-custody death in B.C. in a week.
Police report the man, who was arrested in Surrey on Friday night, died in hospital Tuesday.
Officers said the man had a heart attack when taken into custody and was put on life support in hospital where he later died.
A woman arrested for public intoxication died June 26 while being held at an RCMP facility in the central B.C. city of Prince George.
Just after midnight police received a complaint of a half naked man rolling around in the bushes.
When officers tried to arrest the man for public intoxication, they noticed a female who was also under the influence.
The man and woman were both arrested and placed in cells at the RCMP detachment in Prince George.
Sometime later, while conducting routine prisoner checks an officer discovered the woman was unresponsive in her cell.
Earlier this year, a report prepared by the RCMP in Ottawa found 56% of RCMP in-custody deaths occurred in B.C., even though only a third of the force's officers are stationed in the province.
